Debuchy marchait un peu sur l'eau

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that président de l'US Lesquin (R2), de Padbol France (tennis-ballon) et travaillant aussi pour Stryve (agence de joueurs basée en Suisse), Mathieu Debuchy (41 ans) ne manque pas d'activités depuis qu'il a raccroché les crampons il y a 3 ans dans la plus belle ambiance de France.
  • "Le moment où je me suis senti le plus fort dans ma carrière ?
  • L’entraîneur qui m'a le plus marqué ?

Sources indicate that président de l'US Lesquin (R2), de Padbol France (tennis-ballon) et travaillant aussi pour Stryve (agence de joueurs basée en Suisse), Mathieu Debuchy (41 ans) ne manque pas d'activités depuis qu'il a raccroché les crampons il y a 3 ans dans la plus belle ambiance de France. Dans un intéressant entretien publié aujourd'hui dans Ouest-France, l'ancien défenseur stéphanois évoque notamment ses vertes années. Extraits.

"Le moment où je me suis senti le plus fort dans ma carrière ? Il y a deux phases. La première, c’est quand j’arrive à Newcastle, je me sens très fort. Je fais d’ailleurs une top saison, et je signe à Arsenal après un an et demi. À ce moment, je me sentais vraiment bien, avant que je ne sois freiné brusquement par les blessures à Arsenal, au bout de quelques mois. Puis j’ai eu une renaissance, à Saint-Étienne : après mon arrivée, je marchais un peu sur l’eau pendant quatre ou cinq mois. Ça s’est super bien passé.

L’entraîneur qui m'a le plus marqué ? En ressortir un, c’est compliqué. Je peux ressortir Claude Puel, qui m’a lancé donc, forcément, ça marque. Rudi Garcia, avec qui on a effectué le doublé. Arsène Wenger, évidemment, par son aura et ses qualités d’entraîneur. Si je devais en ressortir un dernier, c’est Jean-Louis Gasset, qui est malheureusement décédé. Il m’a vraiment marqué dans son management, ses qualités humaines, c’était fort.

Mon plus grand regret ? J’ai une petite déception par rapport à la Coupe du monde 2018. J’avais mis les chances de mon côté en allant à Saint-Étienne pour jouer le plus possible. J’ai passé 4-5 mois à donner le maximum et ça s’est très bien passé pour moi. J’étais performant, on a gagné des matches. Malheureusement, je suis resté réserviste. Quand on connaît la finalité, forcément, ça laisse un petit goût amer.".

Access, Not Chances: How Como Took Manchester United Apart – LC

📅 24 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4224 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Spielverlagerung

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • von Next Generation am 24.10.2026 in den Kategorien Champions League,Uncategorized mit 0 Kommentaren.
  • Industry observers note that como beat Manchester United 4-1 — and in this case the scoreline really is a fair expression of the game.
  • Cesc Fàbregas’s side demonstrated two things that rarely go together.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

von Next Generation am 24.10.2026 in den Kategorien Champions League,Uncategorized mit 0 Kommentaren.

Industry observers note that como beat Manchester United 4-1 — and in this case the scoreline really is a fair expression of the game. For long stretches the match was one-sided, not in terms of chance volume but in terms of access: Como dictated in every phase where the ball went, who received it, and under what conditions it had to be played on. United never got on terms in any of those phases.

Cesc Fàbregas’s side demonstrated two things that rarely go together. Out of possession, a pressing structure with clear direction, isolation of one side, and man-marking that applied near the ball only for the action in progress while everything around it was already speculating on the second ball. And in possession, a positional game of remarkable technical maturity that ties opponents in, switches play, and works systematically into the space behind them. The 4-1 is therefore less an outlier than evidence of work that has been built up over recent seasons.

This analysis goes through the phases one by one: first Como in possession and United’s response, then the work against the ball from the high press to defending the box, and finally the goals.

Industry observers note that in build-up, Como moved away from their nominal 4-2-3-1 and sat closer to a 4-3-3, with the eights as the real variable: very free in their movement and above all active in the half-spaces. The base structure stayed stable — a flat four plus a six in front of them, sometimes ahead of the line, sometimes slightly behind the forward line.

Close to their own goal, Como consistently involved goalkeeper Butez as an additional central player in the build-up. That created a five-against-four against United’s front line — awkward on paper, more awkward still in execution, because Como didn’t use the overload to play through but to tie opponents in. From there, the same shape kept appearing on both the right and the left: centre-back, full-back, a player from the half-position in the eight space, and a six alongside. A diamond that wasn’t an end in itself but had a purpose: the diagonal route out.

Como’s build-up structure. From a 4-1 (flat four), the half-positions with Paz and Perrone are added. Small triangles and diamonds emerge. The three attackers ahead of them create additional options in behind.

Recent findings suggest that one detail deserves particular attention. At times the full-backs stood not wide but flat, in a half-position. That sounds like a nuance, but it had a clear function: it vacated the wing and created the space the eights could drop into — Paz and Perrone did so regularly. If you don’t occupy the wing yourself, you force the opponent to guard it anyway.

ManU got no access near the ball and left large diagonal spaces open on the far side.

Industry observers note that for United’s midfielders this was close to unsolvable. Tielemans, Mount and Andrey Santos spent the whole game struggling to establish any responsibility at all, let alone get into duels. When an eight dropped out, they couldn’t follow, and if one of them was tied in by it, a two-against-one opened up on the far wing. Como didn’t create that situation once; they created it serially.

Industry observers note that the decisive mechanism lay in receiving and relaying the ball. The player in the deeper position usually worked with two touches: the first took the ball backwards, the second relayed it to the free teammate. At the end of every one of those actions stood a player with the game in front of him — and from that open position he could switch play.

What made it possible were the preparatory movements. Paz and captain Da Cunha first lured their markers in the wrong direction and then worked with the head start they’d bought. That head start isn’t only space, it’s above all time: time to control the ball first and relay it second, rather than having to do both in one touch.

Industry observers note that A scene in the 17th minute is typical. Mason Mount steps out, Mazraoui goes into the duel at the same time — nominally United are in an overload here. Only neither of them really gets to the opponent, because both are too late. Paz can therefore calmly take his touch backwards and switch play directly with the second, dissolving the pressure before it had even formed.

When the build-up ran down the right, it indicated in a recurring pattern: Paz and Da Cunha took the first touch backwards or inside and then switched with the left foot out of a closed body position. The players they found were systematically in open positions — Milla, the far-side six, or the wing-to-wing connection directly.

In the second half, Como adjusted the shape and more often played with two sixes, to form the diamonds faster and switch to the far-side six faster. Couto stood out in this: the right-back repeatedly played the chip into the six or ten space — six or seven times in a row during one spell. It was mainly Paz who received the ball there and could launch the attack.

In the second half Como focus on those diagonal spaces and look for them mainly with chipped balls.

It has been revealed that especially striking inside the diamond are the rotations between the players. Because of the connections between them, they moved in rotation depending on running path, space and ball movement. The same recurring spaces were re-occupied. Under pressure on the ball carrier, the outer players pushed flat or ran in behind the opponents; the highest player in the diamond burst out of the cover shadow and became the reference point in depth. On a deep pass, the two wide players released and joined the depth, able to offer themselves again immediately in an open body position. If the pass went via the flat wide players, the spaces in front of the new ball carrier could be run into. Every rotation, every positional adjustment was coordinated with the others and, in the end, produced a stream of pressure-resolving passes while Manchester United chased the press in vain.

Sources indicate that como bridged the middle third exceptionally quickly, via dribbles at speed and diagonal passes. Behind it stood a recognisable principle: first tie the opponent to one wing, then get behind them via the diagonal, and in the final third do the same thing again. In sum, that produced the shape of a Z — build-up on the right, transition on the left, finish from the right again.

According to recent reports, in this example Como pin ManU in the press with their short passing. Thanks to the extra attacker on the ball-near side they can play through the pressure and switch.

The connections between wingers and striker carried these attacks and were deliberately kept flexible. The wide players sometimes stayed wide, sometimes came short, sometimes tucked inside. Douvikas accordingly either waited deep in front of the line for the chipped ball or, when space opened up on the wing, received the deeper pass and then ran in behind along the wing as soon as the ball sat on the full-back’s open foot. That flexibility produced the overloads on one side, and the overloads produced the central overload.

In the final third one element was added that is rare in fast transition teams: patience. Como drew opponents towards them with dribbles and short passes, used back-passes when needed, and then switched in front of the block. Da Cunha, Baturina and Paz were the three who could tie opponents in and then find the diagonal. They created the positions on the diagonal, were available to receive, and used their space to apply pressure. The block was usually tied in with short touches, the switch and the position behind the opponent prepared, and quick finishes sought.

It has been revealed that the intensity in possession shouldn’t be underestimated. Practically every attack involved at least three or four players, the width was occupied, the centre likewise, and there were multiple options throughout. What they looked for almost every time was the space behind the opponent on the far side — exactly the zone that is closed last when a block shifts across.

Recent findings suggest that paz brought the right profile for this pattern. A strong left foot cutting inside from the right, he repeatedly dropped into the right-hand blind side of his opponents, got shots away there with few touches, and racked up the most shots of the match. That the finishes generally came off few touches isn’t a detail but the consequence of the time won further back.

According to recent reports, as the move continues, Como again look for the blind side of the defenders. Here Douvikas and Paz are positioned in behind, with Da Cunha joining in front of the back line. After briefly pinning the opponents, the switch reaches Da Cunha, who misses the target from distance.

What carries all of this is the technical execution. Soft passes, sharp ones when the moment called for it, consistently well timed and played into the right foot — for ninety minutes. Passing that secure at that tempo is what makes a variable concept actually retrievable.

Industry observers note that united’s basic problem out of possession was the hybrid. They pressed half man-oriented, but with a plus-one in the last line — a construction that forces compromises in both directions. It demands access up front that it doesn’t fund at the back.

There were certainly moments when it worked. When Dalot pushed through into the press on the right and passed his man backwards, a clean man-orientation emerged all the way up to the front — and with it a clear assignment for Mount, out of which the ball could be won. But that stayed the exception. Most of the time Dalot sat too flat out of possession, so United couldn’t trigger the duels up front and went into the press a man short.

Mount was the most conspicuous case in this respect. He barely got into a duel across the whole match because the decision to step out always came too late. Against a team that works with preparatory movements, a late decision is practically the same as none: the opponent already has the head start before the journey even begins.

In a recent development, on top of that came a problem on the far side. There, United’s winger frequently failed to protect the depth — usually Mbeumo, who jogged back rather than closing the space. But that was precisely the target zone of Como’s diagonal switches. It allowed them to change sides almost at will and regularly find an open structure on the other side.

According to recent reports, the second half brought no improvement. The distances to opponents stayed large, and centrally what was actually intended still didn’t materialise. Michael Carrick’s double change at half-time was meant to bring more physicality to the six with Carlos Baleba, but it didn’t solve the problem — the assignments still didn’t work, the duels in the centre still didn’t happen, and the wide positions dragged the eights out further, which opened new spaces.

In the end the energy simply wasn’t there to press with the necessary intensity. United’s press became increasingly static, and a static press against an opponent with this passing quality yields not a single ball win — it only hands them the starting positions they’re looking for anyway.

Como started the game in a high press and sustained it above all in the first half, with isolated spells after the break too. It was triggered on back-passes and goal kicks — and, remarkably, by their own goals: after every strike the team immediately pushed high again instead of managing the lead in a deeper block.

The steering ran consistently towards United’s left build-up side. The reason is personnel: Harry Maguire played there with his weaker left foot as the outside foot, and next to him stood another right-footer in Noussair Mazraoui on the left. Two right-footers on one build-up side means the ball always has to be taken back inside to play on — exactly where Como were closing the door. The press was usually triggered by the left-sided forward, with the ball ending up at either Maguire or Mazraoui.

Pressing structure after the change in the second half.

Industry observers note that in the centre Como defended man-oriented, with both sixes pushing very high and taking flat passes into United’s midfielders out of the game. That removed the short route through the middle as an option and left the long ball. But the long ball triggered nothing for United: the second balls went to Como practically every time.

That isn’t chance, it’s running work. The sixes consistently tracked the negative pressing paths back, anticipated the long ball early, and were in front of the line before it arrived. Luis Milla covered the most ground of any player on the pitch in this pattern — recovery runs after being played past, doubling up on the ball, attacking the second ball. When the long ball came from Maguire or one of the full-backs, a six was regularly in front of the line with an intense sprint, sealing the centre, taking away the diagonal follow-up passes and attacking the loose balls.

Defending the long ball and extra support on the second ball.

In a recent development, once the ball was on one side, that side was isolated. The near-side forward had access to the centre-back and dropped back a touch when the pass went to the full-back, so that he covered centre-back and six simultaneously and closed the square pass. The far-side forward marked the goalkeeper. That served two functions at once: it took away United’s escape route via the keeper along with the switch, and it kept a player in position for the moment of the turnover.

The double pivot worked in a deliberate half-position. The near-side six stayed tight to his man, the far-side one dropped slightly behind him — securing the space and at the same time establishing access to the far-side centre-back in United’s back three.

The last line defended largely man-for-man in the high press, and very tightly. But the decisive detail is the one that carries the whole concept: the man-marking near the ball applied only to the action in progress. Around it, players were already releasing from their assignments and orienting towards the second ball. That is only retrievable at very high intensity — and it’s the reason United’s forced long balls produced not a single usable moment.

When Como dropped a line, the man-orientation at the second height stayed exceptionally high. Here too the back-pass served as the trigger to push up as a unit and tip back into man-marking. If United were in a closed body position, the Comaschi had already pushed up far enough to attack the back-pass at the moment it was played — a pattern that led directly to the 3-0. The half-position was at work there again: closing down level with the centre-back while simultaneously prepared to push through onto the next player deeper.

In the first half Como still had problems assigning the half-positions against ManU’s 3-2-5. In this example Fernandes moves to the wing, Como fail to establish responsibility and access and are played through at mid-height.

According to recent reports, up to half-time, though, Como had a structural problem with this. The pure man-marking didn’t come off cleanly, because of the two sixes in front of the line, one should really have tucked in and taken over the half-position for the centre-backs. That didn’t happen consistently. The consequence: a centre-back stepped out, the space behind him stayed unoccupied, and that was exactly what United kept attacking.

In a recent development, the pattern of pressing onto Manchester United’s left side continued in the second half, now with Dalot at full-back. The press was still triggered by Douvikas, with the ball-near winger pushing up as a second striker to press the centre-back. Paz focused on the visitors’ ball-near six and Couto pushed through onto Dalot. Through the central connections the game was isolated on one side.

Recent findings suggest that at half-time Como adjusted. One six moved directly into the line, with the far-side winger pushing in onto the six — they now pressed out of a 5-2-1-2. Lucas Da Cunha pressed through from the right onto Maguire, while Nico Paz picked up United’s six. The central forward pressed the central centre-back and from there carried on to the goalkeeper. The far-side wide midfielder and the remaining six were poised — one onto United’s free six, one onto the far-side centre-back — again in that half-position between opponent and the space to be protected.

ManU building up high against the man-oriented Italians.

It has been revealed that the effect was immediately visible. Como controlled the half-positions, got access right into the last line throughout, and set the rhythm of the match from then on. The adjustment solved exactly the problem the first half had left open, without changing the underlying principle.

According to recent reports, in the final phase Como defended from a very deep line inside the box. That left barely any space behind the line to play into — which United hardly looked for anyway. The visitors attacked little depth and rarely occupied the width in the final third, so Como could stay compact without being punished for it.

Accordingly, a lot of players stood very centrally in and in front of the box. That produced numerous cover shadows and a numerical superiority around the ball, which allowed them to steer actively within the block rather than merely react. At times they deliberately steered inside, to guide the opponent into the prepared congestion and cover from a deeper position.

Deep back line in the box, centre closed and play steered inside. The box defending allowed the English side shots from distance.

The crucial point is that Como left the gaps open not despite this set-up but because of it. If you pack the box and secure the depth, you give up the space in front of the line — and that is exactly where United were supposed to shoot from.

It has been revealed that the numbers vindicate the decision. Taking the conceded goal out of the box, Como allowed nine shots from outside the penalty area across ninety minutes, worth roughly 0.24 xG combined; only three of them were even on target. On top of that, of the four shots inside the box, two came from at least 14 to 15 metres and effectively belong in the long-range category as well. United accepted the invitation, and the shooting quality was perfectly decent — it’s just that with that scoring probability over a whole match, the most likely outcome is precisely what happened.

Tracking the ball for the first goal.

It has been revealed that 1-0, Nico Paz (2′) — The goal comes before United are even set. Como take the goal kick swiftly and play straight to the full-back, luring the visitors into the press — only not cleanly. Mason Mount triggers the pressure and is played past, and on the second ball he goes into the duel as well instead of holding the middle and looking for the space where he could pick the ball up. That is exactly what opens the centre, the space for the second ball is there, and Paz can play it through.

What follows is the transition principle in its purest form: a quick switch to the diagonal side, then short passes against a very deep line. Matheus Cunha doesn’t pick up the player behind him and leaves the ten space open, where Paz is standing. He needs two touches because neither Cunha from above nor Maguire from his distance gets into the duel. Lammens, for his part, doesn’t defend the goal with his cover shadow but takes the near post — which leaves the far corner to a strong left foot. The curled finish into it is quality, though.

2-0, Anastasios Douvikas (49′, assist Paz) — Same zone, same cause. Bryan Mbeumo doesn’t choose to shut the centre but closes the centre-back, which creates the space for Da Cunha, who drives forward and plays Martin Baturina in. Centrally, Mount again fails to pick up his man. Out wide, Amad Diallo, introduced at half-time, generates no pressure centrally, so Mazraoui can’t take over the deep wide player in the first place.

Recent findings suggest that the result is Paz behind the opponent, in the ten space, dribbling unopposed at goal. Matthijs de Ligt establishes no reference to Douvikas’s run in behind and slips as well — a one-against-one with the goalkeeper that Douvikas finishes coolly.

3-0, Nico Paz (57′) — The only goal that comes directly out of the work against the ball. Como are in the midfield press in a closed position with access to the inside lane, win the ball there and punish a lapse of concentration in the visitors’ build-up. At the end, Paz is alone in front of Lammens again.

4-0, Jacobo Ramón (76′, assist Kaiki) — This goal comes from a longer possession spell and reveals the assignment problem in its clearest form. Mazraoui is too narrow and has no access to the wide player. Diallo stands in the space with access to neither the central player nor the full-back nor the winger — an orientation that doesn’t work in any direction.

Como switch to Máximo Perrone, who can slide the ball out wide because the space is simply free. From there comes the cross from an open body position, and in the centre Como run a two-against-one at the end of which Ramón scores.

According to recent reports, 4-1, Joshua Zirkzee (90′) — Como’s only lapse, and one in a phase in which the team had already dropped very deep. United get the ball to the wing, it’s two against two in the box, and the cross is initially only feinted. Zirkzee orients himself well forwards at that moment, while Como’s defenders are already stepping out after the feinted cross. Diallo’s ball in behind the line is strong, the offside call is razor-thin in his favour, and Zirkzee takes two touches before finishing one-against-one with the goalkeeper. A blemish, not a structural problem.

In a recent development, the common denominator — Three of Como’s four goals come in the same zone: the space in front of and behind United’s line that nobody takes responsibility for. Mount is involved in two of those scenes through an assignment he never establishes, Diallo in two more after coming on. Nico Paz is at the heart of three of the four goals, twice as scorer, once as the provider — always out of the opponent’s blind side.

Como’s 4-1 has one common cause across every phase, and it lies less in any single idea than in its execution under continuous load. Out of possession they steered, isolated and speculated on the second ball — with man-marking that applied near the ball only for the action in progress and was already dissolved around it. In possession they tied opponents in, switched play and worked systematically into the space behind. Both require eleven players to anticipate a teammate’s decision, and both functioned over the full distance.

Sources indicate that the connecting detail is the half-position. In the press, the far-side six stood between opponent and the space to be protected; in possession, the eights worked out of the same zone, and the full-backs occupied it flat in order to vacate the wing for exactly those players. Como, in other words, occupied the position in both directions from which two jobs can be done at once — which is why the side could neither be played past in the press nor be pinned in the build-up.

In a recent development, for United the diagnosis is more uncomfortable than the result. The problem wasn’t individual errors but that the team never, in any phase, got into the duels it needed. The mixture of half man-orientation and a plus-one in the last line funded no access up front, and without access every decision is made too late — from Mount in the centre to Mbeumo failing to secure the far-side depth. Carrick’s double change at half-time was meant to bring physicality to the six with Carlos Baleba, but it changed nothing about the assignments, and in Diallo a player came on wide who reached neither one opponent nor the other in his space. That the energy ran out in the end was a consequence rather than a cause.

It has been revealed that that leaves the context. A 4-1 against Manchester United is no proof in itself, and Como’s finishing was exceptionally efficient on the night. What demonstrated regardless of the result, though, is a team with a recognisable, rehearsed answer in all four phases of the game — and one that put a technical maturity on the pitch in possession that you wouldn’t readily credit to a side promoted two years ago.

Sans doute le moins connu des supporters stéphanois car il n'a joué qu'une demi-heure en équipe première, lors d'un match amical à huis clos (et même pas diffusé par le club) facilement gagné (4-0) à Divonne-les-Bains contre l'équipe B de Lausanne le 29 juillet dernier.

S'étant officiellement engagé avec les Verts il y a 3 mois pile poil, Jediaél Mbambi n'a disputé que 4 matches officiels (en tant que titulaire et dans leur intégralité). Solide lors de son unique rencontre disputée avec la réserve lors de la 1ère journée de N2 (0-0 sur le terrain du Gallia Lucciana), le matru a joué 3 matches avec les U19 : après avoir perdu (0-2) à Béziers, il s'est illustré en mettant un doublé lors du carton (7-0) contre Borgo et en se montrant intraitable lors du succès à Colomiers (2-0).

In a recent development, le grand frère du très prometteur Jeffrey (avant-centre de 15 ans surclassé en équipe de Belgique U17) n'a pas joué cet automne car il a été victime d'un tacle à la cheville. Opéré avec succès, il espère faire son retour sur les terrains en janvier prochain. En attendant, on lui souhaite un prompt rétablissement !

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Feyenoord preserved their four-point advantage over champions PSV after coming away with a point from Eindhoven thanks to an improved second-half performance.

PSV dominated the first half as they deployed a close-passing, tiki-taka style to stifle Feyenoord, but only had Guus Til’s well-taken volley after 20 minutes to show for it.

Ten minutes after the break Feyenoord equalised when Anis Hadj Moussa was given too much space to charge down the right flank and bend a shot inside the far post.

The Algerian had a good chance for a second towards the end, while PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar had to be alert to keep out a header by Nacho Ferri from close range.

“We were by far the better team today and had the better chances,” said PSV coach Peter Bosz. “We started the second half badly and made a mistake, after which Hadj Moussa scored. And even then we could have won it.”.

Ajax overtook PSV to close the gap at the top to three points with a hard-fought win at Sparta. Veteran striker Jens Toornstra scored for Sparta on his 500th Eredivisie appearance, but Abdellah Ouazane and Tolu Arokodare, the scorers against Atalanta in midweek, were on target again to claim the win for Ajax.

Twente moved up to fourth place as two late goals by Sondre Ørjasæter and Lucas Vennegoor of Hesselink earned a 2-0 win at AZ Alkmaar, who like Twente and PSV have 20 points.

Fortuna Sittard also snatched the points late on against Excelsior as Rodrigo Guth headed in a corner in injury time to keep the Limburg club in sixth place, two points further back.

At the other end of the table, the return of Adrie Koster as veteran coach brought no relief to Willem II, who crashed to a 6-1 home defeat to Cambuur.

The Tilburgers remain four points behind ADO Den Haag, who were unable to keep up the momentum of last week’s win against PSV as they lost 3-2 at home to Heerenveen.

Telstar lost by the same margin at Go Ahead Eagles, whose striker Søren Tengstedt netted twice in the first half to lead the Eredivisie scoring charts with eight goals.

Willem II Tilburg 1-6 Cambuur Leeuwarden.

Sports club members becoming less tolerant of homosexuality

📅 27 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (274 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dutchnews

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.
  • See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.
  • Acceptance of homosexuality in Dutch sports clubs has declined significantly in the last generation, according to a survey of attitudes by the Mulier Institute.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Acceptance of homosexuality in Dutch sports clubs has declined significantly in the last generation, according to a survey of attitudes by the Mulier Institute.

The organisation found that 66% of people had no objection to a fellow member of a sports club being gay, while in 2008 the figure was 85%.

Just over half (55%) of respondents said they had no problem sharing a shower with a gay team-mate of the same sex, which also represented a drop from 73% in 2008.

The Mulier Institute said the findings reflected a social trend that has also been seen in schools, where the proportion of boys aged between 12 and 16 with a positive view of homosexuality has dropped from 40% to 22% since 2021.

The Dutch Olympic Committee NOC*NSF said the findings were “highly regrettable” and pledged to step up its efforts to make sport more inclusive.

But the John Blankenstein Foundation, which campaigns for LGBT emancipation in sport, stated it had noticed declining enthusiasm for its workshops and growing numbers of parents who voiced objections.

Karin Blankenstein, who set up the organisation in 2008, told NOS: “I get the sensitivity around transgender people in sport at the top level, but this is about amateur sport.”.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

A late equaliser for Fortuna Sittard in De Kuip proved costly for Feyenoord as PSV and Twente racked up huge victories to move within two points of the Eredivisie leaders.

Feyenoord paid the price for failing to finish off the Limburgers, with Luciano Valente’s 59th-minute goal the only reward for their dominance.

Fortuna equalised with four minutes left when Shiloh ’t Zand, on loan from Feyenoord, was allowed to run through to the penalty area and beat Tjark Ernst with a low shot.

Recent findings suggest that feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst made no effort to hide his disappointment. “We know that Fortuna are the kind of team who can score from the few attacks they have,” he mentioned. “If you don’t score the goals, things like this can happen.”.

Second-placed Ajax are a point behind after a narrow win at home against AZ ended an 11-match winless streak against the Alkmaar club, as Tolu Arokodare’s early header proved decisive.

Twente recorded the biggest win of the weekend with a 9-0 demolition of Excelsior in Rotterdam, with Wout Weghorst scoring four times and Sondre Ørjasaeter notching up five assists.

It has been revealed that excelsior collapsed following the fifth-minute dismissal of Nesto Groen for a reckless high challenge. The home side were 5-0 down at half-time, with Weghorst claiming a hat-trick in the opening 33 minutes.

PSV bagged seven goals in a one-sided encounter with bottom club Willem II, with all the goals coming from different scorers including Ricardo Pepi, who came on in the second half after a six-week absence through injury.

Telstar opened up a three-point gap at the bottom over ADO Den Haag with a 4-2 win against Utrecht in a painful return to Velsen-Zuid for Telstar’s former coach Anthony Correia.

ADO went down 1-0 in Zwolle, with PEC’s Dylan Mbayo scoring the only goal with a first-time finish on the stroke of half-time.

The match between Cambuur Leeuwarden and Go Ahead Eagles was suspended in the 82nd minute after visiting fans threw fireworks onto the pitch.

The clubs agreed with the KNVB not to play the final minutes and allow Cambuur’s 4-0 advantage to stand as the final result.

Go Ahead’s director Jan-Willem van Dop noted the club would take action against those responsible: “I am ashamed on behalf a small group of supporters who ruined things for the club and a large hare of the fans in the away end,” he said.

Cambuur Leeuwarden 4-0 Go Ahead Eagles.

Dual passports issue continues to plague Dutch-based footballers

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (569 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dutchnews

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.
  • See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.
  • Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.

Suriname’s parliament passed a law in September enabling players who are selected for the national team to gain citizenship automatically.

But the Dutch immigration service IND remarked the law passed in Suriname made no difference to the rules on dual nationality in the Netherlands.

“The fact that Surinamese nationality has been obtained by legal means is not enough on its own to qualify for one of the exceptional categories under our law,” a spokesman for the Dutch justice ministry told broadcaster NOS.

The law was intended to settle the question of dual nationality for footballers, which arose last March when NAC Breda challenged the eligibility of Go Ahead Eagles defender Dean James.

James took Indonesian citizenship last year after accepting an invitation to play for the national team, but under Dutch dual nationality rules he was required to give up his original passport.

The Dutch football association KNVB debuted an investigation into the employment status of players who were called up by countries such as Suriname, Cape Verde and Indonesia. In the meantime it arranged for Dutch-based players to be given temporary work permits so they could keep playing for their clubs.

Losing Dutch nationality also stripped them of their EU citizenship, meaning they would need to obtain visas and meet stricter criteria, such as an annual salary threshold of €600,000, to be eligible to play in the Eredivisie.

Several players have passed up invitations to join the Surinamese squad because of the uncertainty, including Danilho Doekhi of Lazio, Milan van Ewijk of Coventry City and Jayden Oosterwolde of Fenerbahçe.

National team manager Henk Fraser said it was “inexplicable” that players’ livelihoods were being damaged by their desire to play international football.

“Both countries have to get together and clarify the situation,” he told NOS. “This is a straightforward case of people following their hearts and wanting to play for Suriname, but not knowing where they stand.”.

Some players said they felt misled by the Surinamese football association, which told them they were playing for the national team on “sports passports” that allowed them to remain Dutch citizens.

Former Feyenoord winger Jean-Paul Boëtius noted he only discovered after he was first called up for Suriname last year that he had inadvertently renounced his Dutch citizenship as a result.

Shortly afterwards he received a letter from the city council in Rotterdam telling him to hand in his Dutch passport, which he had recently renewed, because it was no longer valid.

According to recent reports, “I now have a sticker in my Surinamese passport that indicates I have a residency permit allowing me to live in the Netherlands,” he told NOS. “But that’s only for a year. It’s a very difficult situation. I want to become Dutch again. I was born and brought up here.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il governatore dice di averne parlato con Tajani e chiede al presidente biancoceleste di misurare il proprio consenso.

In a recent development, francesco Rocca invita Claudio Lotito a candidarsi con Forza Italia alle comunali di Roma del 2027, per misurare il consenso che saprebbe raccogliere. Secondo quanto riportato da Lacapitale, Il presidente della Regione Lazio rivolge la sfida al senatore e presidente biancoceleste durante «Nexus – Visioni e strategie di sviluppo del territorio», la manifestazione in corso al Palacongressi di Fiuggi, come riferisce La Capitale. Rocca riassume così la sua proposta: «Lotito si candidi a Roma con Forza Italia, così vediamo quanti voti prende, forse qualcuno anche dai romanisti».

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Rocca, tifoso della Lazio e da tempo critico verso la gestione societaria di Lotito, porta così il confronto anche sul piano politico. Le sue parole non sono un annuncio di candidatura da parte di Lotito né una proposta formalizzata dalla coalizione di centrodestra.

Il governatore chiama in causa il segretario nazionale di Forza Italia, Antonio Tajani, al quale dice di aver già prospettato una candidatura di Lotito nella Capitale. Collega l’ipotesi alla volontà del presidente della Lazio di proseguire la propria attività politica e al ritorno delle preferenze.

«Ho detto al presidente di Forza Italia Antonio Tajani: visto che Lotito si è innamorato della politica, vuole continuare ed è legittimo, e considerato che tornano le preferenze, dovrebbe candidarlo a Roma», afferma Rocca.

According to recent reports, all’invito aggiunge una battuta sulla rivalità tra le due squadre romane: «Così vediamo quante ne prende, forse qualcuna anche dai romanisti». Il punto della sfida, per Rocca, è verificare i voti che Lotito otterrebbe attraverso una candidatura personale.

Recent findings suggest that il presidente della Regione lega la prova elettorale al ruolo che, a suo giudizio, la Lazio ha avuto nel percorso politico di Lotito. «Questo è il momento della verità per Lotito, per dimostrare che è lui un valore aggiunto per la politica, altrimenti è vero il contrario: è stata la Lazio a portarlo in Senato», sostiene.

Industry observers note that rocca insiste sull’opportunità di cominciare dalle amministrative romane con Forza Italia e richiama anche Reggio Calabria. «Oggi ha la possibilità di dimostrare che la Lazio ha portato tanti consensi a lui e al suo partito. È andato a Reggio Calabria? Si candidasse a Roma, accettasse la sfida, cominciasse già dalle comunali con Forza Italia e vediamo quanto è trascinatore di folle».

In a recent development, le dichiarazioni si collocano nel confronto politico in vista delle elezioni capitoline del 2027. Restano, però, una sfida lanciata da Rocca a Lotito, non una candidatura annunciata dal presidente biancoceleste.

Au cours d'un match plaisant, les Verts se sont imposés en Champagne 1 but à 0 grâce au meilleur joueur de L2 la saison passée, Zuriko Davitashvili.

Le Géorgien n'était pas titulaire au coup d'envoi. Ian Cathro privilégiant la continuité en attaque avec le quatuor Ballo - Breum - Boakye - Cardona. Derrière, Pedro et Le Cardinal occupaient la charnière et Ferreira / Old, les côtés.

Si les Verts étaient rapidement sauvé par Csongvai qui contrait in extremis un tir remois dans la surface, ils allaient toutefois se procurer de belles occasions. Sur un centre de Cardona, Ballo ratait sa tête en cherchant à remiser pour Breum face au but. Plus tard, ce fut Boakye qui décochait une belle frappe captée par le gardien. Enfin, sur un centre venu de la droite, Cardona reprenait en retrait en première intention mais sa frappe rasait le montant.

Au retour des vestiaires, Reims se faisait plus pressant. Les Champenois allaient même se créer une belle occasion. Tia enrhumait Pedro mais sa frappe trouvait un Ndiaye impeccable, Fofana ne pouvait pas cadrer sur le second ballon.

Recent findings suggest that ce fut au tour des Verts de reprendre la main avec un mouvement collectif sublime. Csongvai trouvait Breum qui s'appuyait sur Cardona qui alertait Boakye à gauche. Le centre ras terre devant le but trouvait Davitashvili qui n'avait plus qu'à pousser au fond des buts (0-1, 61e).

Les Verts cadenassaient la défense et procédaient en contre sans parvenir à doubler la mise malgré de belles situations.

Cette 2e défaite de la saison pour les Remois permet à l'ASSE de reprendre 3 points d'avance sur Nancy en tête de la L2 et de porter son avance à 10 points sur son adversaire du soir, et 7 sur le 3e, Montpellier, battu à Laval.

Le résumé vidéo de la victoire des Verts à Reims est à voir ici.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Feyenoord are facing a heavy fine from European football authorities after fireworks were let off during their Champions League defeat by Internazionale.

It has been revealed that referee Glenn Nyberg suspended the match for several minutes after flares were fired onto the roof from outside De Kuip stadium, damaging the structure. Police later made two arrests.

“It’s obviously not right and it’ll be another fine,” coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst said wearily after the game, which ended in a comprehensive 3-0 defeat for his team.

One flare landed on the pitch despite the club taking measures such as hanging nets from the gantries to stop objects being thrown from the stands. “They’re letting off fireworks from outside now,” Van Bronckhorst said. “What do you do about that?”.

Uefa are likely to hit Feyenoord with a fine and could order the club to close parts of the stadium for their next home matches in the competition, against Porto on November 24 and RB Leipzig on January 27.

The club also have a suspended penalty hanging over them from last October, when they were fined €60,000 after fans let off fireworks during the match against Greek club Panathinaikos.

On the pitch, Feyenoord were undone by a classic display of Italian defending and counter-attacking, as Internazionale sat back after taking an eighth-minute lead through Yann Bisseck.

Francesco Pio Esposito headed in a second early in the second half, just as Feyenoord were pushing for an equaliser, before Piotr Zielinski made sure of the win with a shot from 20 metres.

Captain Luciano Valente said the result was “more than deserved” and the visitors had shown more “quality”.

Sources indicate that “This defeat was harder to take than the one against Barcelona,” he told Ziggo Sport. “Because we thought going in that we could get something, but we just weren’t good enough.”.

Van Bronckhorst said he was not surprised by the difference in class between the teams. “They scored the first goal out of nothing,” he said. “And Inter know better what the game needs at every stage.

Industry observers note that “Their players have a lot of experience, they’ve been in the final twice in the last four years. So we’re at a disadvantage.”.

L'Union rapporte les propos de l'entraîneur rémois Nicolas Usaï après la première défaite à domicile de la saison de son équipe, désormais à 10 longueurs de ses bourreaux d'hier, les solides leaders stéphanois.

According to recent reports, "Il y a de la déception par rapport à l’engagement que l’on a mis dans le match. On sait que ça se joue sur des détails, on a concédé peu d’occasions par rapport à la faculté de notre adversaire. On n’a pas été assez efficaces dans nos moments forts, particulièrement dans les 25 premières minutes. Après le but, on a manqué un peu d’allant, peut-être un peu d’énergie. On savait que c’était une opposition de qualité. Rien à reprocher aux joueurs dans le comportement, dans l’engagement.

La maîtrise était stéphanoise. Dans le coeur du jeu, ils ont réussi à éteindre rapidement les quelques étincelles que l’on a pu avoir. On est déçus par rapport au résultat. Quand on joue dans un stade comme ça, avec de nombreux supporters, on a envie de pouvoir communier avec eux à la fin et ce n’est pas le cas. Par rapport au peu d’occasions que l’on a subies, c’est très frustrant.

Saint-Étienne fait un écart, Nancy a encore gagné, Montpellier avait perdu, c’était l’occasion de repasser devant... On est à la 13e journée et au-delà du classement, il faut être lucide par rapport à ce ce que l’on est en capacité de faire, même s’il faut rester mesuré, ne pas être alarmiste. Là, la défaite à Grenoble fait encore plus mal.".

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

PSV Eindhoven endured a frustrating night in the Champions League as their defensive frailties were exposed in a 2-1 defeat by Club Brugge.

PSV started full of attacking intent and should have taken an early lead when Ivan Perisic put Sergiño Dest clean through on goal, but the defender’s shot was too close to goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

Instead it was the visitors who took the lead with their first real attack when Nicolo Tresoldi headed in a teasing cross from Joaquin Seys.

Sources indicate that PSV equalised early in the second half as an outstanding pass by Sven Mijnans into the path Lutsharel Geertruida allowed the defender to charge to the byline. His pullback found its way to Kodai Sano, whose shot took a deflection off Seys into the net.

But five minutes later PSV were caught out as another razor-sharp pass by Seys released Carlos Forbs in space to net the winner.

The home side refused to give up, but were unable to find a way past Sommer in the closing stages as the Belgian side closed out the win.

According to recent reports, team captain Mauro Junior admitted that PSV had been undone by shortcomings at the back. “We had a lot of opportunities in the first half but we didn’t score,” he told Ziggo Sport.

“We want to attack and score goals, but we weren’ well organised today in defence. We need to keep our heads up and look forward to the next game.”.

The result leaves PSV in 24th place, just above the elimination line, ahead of their next match away to Real Madrid on November 24, with four points from their opening four matches.

Marquer cinq minutes après être entré en jeu, forcément, c’est spécial. Ça m’a aidé à retrouver le rythme, et je suis vraiment heureux d’avoir inscrit ce but.".

As part of PortuGOAL’s efforts to constantly evolve and serve lovers of Portuguese football with top-quality and increasingly accessible content, we are replacing the PortuGOAL Android and Apple APPs with a new Progressive Web Application (PWA) as from tomorrow, Tuesday 3 April.

This massive step forward in phone apps technology loads the content instantly, even in areas of low connectivity, stays up to date at all times, displays the most recent version upon launching, is more efficient than native apps, works on-demand and is always accessible, without taking up a smartphone’s valuable memory or data. This is a football site, not a technology one, but for those of you of a techy nature, click here for more on why PWAs are the future of phone applications.

In another improvement, the website itself will be implementing SSL technology at the same time, leading to more secure and faster navigation. PortuGOAListas should be directed to the upcoming URL automatically from tomorrow, if not simply type http://portugoal.net into your browser’s address bar then bookmark the page. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

La capolista affronta il Lecce, fermo a 10 punti; la squadra di Gasperini trova il Parma, a quota otto.

Lazio e Roma possono allungare a 12 giornate il loro primato congiunto di imbattibilità nel prossimo turno di Serie A. Dopo la sosta per le Nazionali, il campionato 2026-27 riprende con la dodicesima giornata, in programma dal 21 al 23 novembre 2026. Le due squadre capitoline giocheranno entrambe sabato 21 novembre.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Come riportato da Opta, Lazio e Roma sono rimaste entrambe imbattute nelle prime 11 giornate per la prima volta nella storia delle formazioni romane nella massima serie. Il risultato raggiunto prima della pausa può quindi essere migliorato nel prossimo turno: se nessuna delle due perderà, la serie condivisa salirà a 12 giornate.

Sources indicate that le partite delle due squadre sono concentrate nello spazio di poche ore. Alle 15 la Lazio ospiterà il Lecce all’Olimpico; alle 18 toccherà alla Roma, impegnata sul campo del Parma. Saranno questi i due incontri da cui dipenderà la possibilità di prolungare il primato congiunto.

Y'en a Marne ! (3)

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (331 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Poteaux-carres

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Dans sa dernière édition, L'Union revient sur la déplorable absence des supporters stéphanois dans le parcage du stade Auguste-Delaune.
  • In a recent development, "Selon nos informations, un nouvel encadrement des supporters stéphanois a été créé par les autorités le matin même du match.
  • Sources indicate that mais l'information n'a pas le temps de circuler.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dans sa dernière édition, L'Union revient sur la déplorable absence des supporters stéphanois dans le parcage du stade Auguste-Delaune. Extraits.

In a recent development, "Selon nos informations, un nouvel encadrement des supporters stéphanois a été créé par les autorités le matin même du match. Des autobus neutres accueillis à un péage sur le parcours et escortés jusqu'au stade. C'est d'ailleurs pour cela qu'ils sont partis. Le parcage d'Auguste-Delaune, de nouveau ouvert, et le Stade de Reims, étaient de nouveau prêts à les faire venir. Et ce, quelques heures avant le coup d'envoi du match. Sauf que la préfecture de la Marne, que nous avons contactée, ne l'a pas entendu de cette oreille et maintient : tout transport véhiculant des Stéphanois entrant dans le département sera intercepté et le parcage visiteur reste fermé.

Sources indicate that mais l'information n'a pas le temps de circuler. Le Stade de Reims l'apprend au dernier moment, pareil pour les supporters stéphanois déjà partis en bus. Certains rebroussent chemin, d'autres persistent. Ce qui donne une scène assez folle au péage de Champfleury, au sud de la Cité des Sacres. Les bus et minibus sont arrêtés par les forces de l'ordre et sommés de retourner d'où ils viennent. Près de 6 heures pour l'aller et la même chose pour le retour. Pour ces supporters, la rencontre se regardera sur la route... Cruel.

Ce qui n'est pas le cas d'autres, plus malins, qui avaient pris leur ticket dans d'autres tribunes, notamment tout proche du parcage resté vide. Munis d'ailleurs sous leur blouson de maillot et d'écharpe aux couleurs de l'ASSE, jusque-là bien cachés, mais qui ont été ressortis au coup d'envoi. Ceux-là, plusieurs centaines, ont pu donner de la voix, surtout après la victoire de leur club. Mais l'ambiance aurait pu prendre plus d'ampleur avec la présence de leurs partenaires. C'est quand même mieux un stade garni...".

La Préfecture de la Marne a manifestement oublié les grands principes de la Répubique : liberté, égalité, fraternité.

Hier les U16 de Kevin De Jesus étaient exempts de la 9ème journée de leur championnat (poule B), tout comme l'US Annecy le Vieux dans ce même championnat (poule B). c'était donc l'occasion pour les deux clubs respectifs de programmer une rencontre amicale. Ce qui fut fait, hier après-midi, à l'Etrat. L'occasion aussi pour les Verts de renouer avec la victoire (1-0) après la défaite de la semaine dernière à Andrézieux.

Malgré plusieurs situations de but, les Verts ont dû patienter jusqu'à la 40ème minute pour ouvrir la marque : suite à une perte de balle de balle de la défense annecienne, de l'entrée de la surface Noah Fontaine. plaçait une frappe enroulée qui faisait mouche. Ce sera le score à la mi-temps et également le score final, même si les Verts, sérieux et plutôt dominateurs auraient pu alourdir le score, avec un peu plus de justesse dans la finition.

Industry observers note that la réaction de Kevin De Jesus : "Dans l'ensemble nous avons eu la possession, face à une équipe qui a joué en bloc bas. Il est dommage de ne pas avoir concrétiser les situations que nous nous sommes créées. Mais ce match permet aux jeunes de rester dans le rythme, il permet aussi de donner du temps de jeu à ceux qui en avaient moins et d'intégrer les joueurs revenant de blessure".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well.
  • In a recent development, getting started on football betting is far from easy, though.
  • According to recent reports, but experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well. Especially popular in Europe, betting on football can be an incredibly profitable enterprise, so long as you know how to do it.

In a recent development, getting started on football betting is far from easy, though. This form of gambling requires dedication, investment, and persistence. As you gain experience, your intuition will improve and you will be able to make more correct predictions.

According to recent reports, but experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter. In fact, you can substantially improve your betting strategy by simply following some basic football betting tips.

You might find shopping around boring and unhelpful, but you just have to do it when you search sites for football betting. As you know, the higher the odds, the bigger the payout. What you may have missed, however, is that odds are different at each bookmaker. Having remarked that, shopping around for the best odds is sensible, as it rewards you with bigger payouts.

According to recent reports, in this line of thought, sticking to one bookmaker is virtually pointless. Even if the bookie of your choosing offers the best odds for a number of matches, it is highly unlikely that their odds will remain the best for long.

Sources indicate that an obvious one, we know. And yet, you will be surprised by the number of football bettors who wager on football, but do not follow the sport. So, why is it key to follow the action closely?

First of all, by watching football matches, you can take part in the most exciting football betting market – the live betting market. What is more important, however, is that following the action provides an invaluable insight into teams and players’ style, condition, and determination – important factors  to consider when placing a bet.

Recent findings suggest that as you watch more and more games, you will improve your analytic abilities. In time, you will be able to make more accurate predictions about the outcome of different matches, which, of course,  will result in placing more winning bets.

It has been revealed that as you know, odds are based on the probability of occurrence of a certain outcome; the higher the odds, the more unlikely it is for that outcome to actually occur. But what happens when the odds offered by the bookmaker represent a probability that is lower than the actual probability of an outcome occurring? In such a situation, you can place what is called a value bet.

If you want to become a professional football punter, you should always search for value when betting, as it leads to huge profits.

In a recent development, favoured by beginners in particular, accumulators are a type of football wager which allows you to bet on as many fixtures as you like. Most commonly, you will be asked to choose a match winner, but as the market is diverse, you may be offered a number of other betting options. What makes accumulators an appealing betting market is the huge potential payout – here, you can stake as little as £1 and have the potential to win more than £500,000, depending on the bookmaker and the number of selected fixtures.

Industry observers note that if you find accumulators’ payouts too good to be true, you are right. As a matter of fact, there is a reason for the odds to be set so high – actually winning an accumulator bet, especially one which involves a wide selection of matches, is nearly impossible. You see, all you need for your whole wager to lose is one wrong prediction. For example, if you bet on 10 matches and just one of them goes wrong, your entire accumulator is lost.

To make money by betting on football, avoid betting on accumulators – the risk is simply not worth it.

Finally, if you want to be a successful football punter, learn how not to mix emotions with betting. This is easier said than done, though.

In a recent development, whenever your favourite team plays, you want them to win, regardless of how (im)possible that may be. If you do not learn how to leave emotions out of betting, however, you are highly likely to put money on your favourite team even if they have no chance of winning the match. Conversely, should you base your bets on hard facts and not on emotions, you increase your chances to win.

Our advice – avoid betting on fixtures that involve one of your favourite teams, that is the easiest way to keep emotions at bay.

PSV returned to the top of the Eredivisie with a thumping 5-2 win over Cambuur Leeuwarden as previous leaders Feyenoord lost a seven-goal thriller against the other Frisian club, Heerenveen.

It took just 46 seconds for PSV to get off the mark as Sven Mijnans headed in unmarked.

The midfielder added a second after 15 minutes and completed his hat-trick with a free-kick in the 80th minute to make the score 4-2, just as Cambuur were threatening a comeback.

Feyenoord’s dip in form continued as they let a two-goal lead slip at Heerenveen. The Rotterdammers looked to be in control going into the break with a trademark drilled shot by Anis Hadj Moussa and a penalty by Nacho Ferri.

But Maas Willemsen bundled in the ball from a corner on the stroke of half-time, before Ringo Meerveld came on for the second half and scored a hat-trick as Feyenoord’s defence crumbled under pressure.

Industry observers note that “In the matches when we played well I saw a team that fought for each other,” Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst said after the game. “Mentally strong, kept running even when we didn’t have the ball. That’s our strength. When we don’t do that we’re a lesser team.”.

Mexx Meerdink scored a hotly contested late penalty to settle a tempestuous game in Alkmaar as AZ came back from 3-1 down against Groningen to claim their first win in five matches.

Sources indicate that goalkeeper Etienne Vaessen was given a second yellow card for protesting too hard against the decision to penalise him for upending Ayoub Oufkir. Once the commotion died down Meerdink, who had missed from the spot against Vaessen earlier in the second half, made no mistake against substitute goalkeeper Lovro Stubljar.

Ajax missed the chance to take over top spot at Twente as their former striker Wout Weghorst scored a last-minute penalty to rescue a point for the home side.

Ajax had been 2-0 up with a bullet header by their giant striker Tolu Arokodare and a long-range strike by Rayane Bounida, before an own goal by Dies Janse brought the visitors back into the game.

According to recent reports, fortuna Sittard also had to settle for a point against Telstar after going 2-0 up thanks to a bizarre own goal by Sem Valk. The defender’s sliced clearance looped over the head of Ronald Koeman Junior as the goalkeeper tried to head it away rather than risk being penalised for handling a backpass.

Goals just before half-time by Abdelnour Soualhia and Patrick Brouwer brought Telstar back into the game, but neither side was able to find a winner after the break.

That result allowed ADO, under the guidance of interim coach Levi Schwiebbe, to close the gap on 16th-placed Telstar to one point with a 3-1 win against Sparta, while bottom Willem II collected their third point of the season at home to PEC Zwolle.

#118855. Opinion: The morality of football

Opinion: The morality of football

📅 08 Jun 2023 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1287 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Portugoal

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.
  • That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.
  • It has been revealed that nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.

Is football a moral force for good? That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.

It has been revealed that nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly. Is there a greater significance to the game we are watching, or is it merely 22 humans kicking a leather ball into a net?

Join Nathan as he elaborates on the most significant takeaways of what was a fascinating discussion on the sport and morality in general.

Football, for some, may be the most poignant reminder of the moral universe in which we live. While debate has raged for centuries regarding the precise origin of moral absolutes and how humans ought to live, it is simply unavoidable to say humanity is often troubled by events surrounding the game we all love so dearly.

In not so distant history, every normal act of human life would have been assigned some degree of moral significance. Every action had inherently moral indicators - for good or for evil. Today, postmodern views of morality dominate. These describe morality as an entirely subjective dimension. In other words, it cannot be pinned down exactly whether behaviors are objectively good or bad. We can only find fault with someone else’s interpretation based on their own unique moral code. Morality is relative to the individual or society.

Yet last night’s dialogue concerning football and human behavior was filled with moral accusations and claims which strongly suggested humans are not content with relativist morality. Indeed, we are at times frightened by and disgusted with what we observe in and around football. Our sense of moral justice is deeply disturbed. But with respect to what exactly?

Industry observers note that in responding to the panelist’s questions, I observed a familiar paradigm. Each time I have discussed any aspect of moral behavior, the speculation humans are good or at worst morally neutral animals continually reemerges. This widely accepted presupposition is then followed shortly by disgust at some aspect of human behavior. Almost as if to ask “why are all these good humans behaving so badly?” while ignoring the very real implications of this line of inquiry. A question rendered unanswerable by the insistent a priori assumptions from which it was derived.

If humans are intrinsically beneficent, conscientious, fair, humble, and honest then why is football rife with racism, misogyny, greed, disenfranchisement, lies, cheating, violence, and the hypocrisy to deny the occurrence of any such behaviors except when a rival club is the guilty party? Behaviors which are perpetrated by individual supporters, fanatical groups, club administrations, corporate bodies such as FIFA, political entities, nations, and even the players themselves. No one participating faction is guiltless.

In a recent development, to so blithely sidestep more sufficient explanations for the empirical reality of wickedness in football and in human behavior more generally is not just factually incorrect. It undermines real attempts to understand the root of these behaviors where they might be dealt with more effectively.

To listen to The Moral Maze episode entitled “Football: a moral force for good?” produced by BBC radio and featuring PortuGOAL’s Seleção correspondent Nathan Motz click on this link.

Sources indicate that furthermore, in good faith, how successful is a response against heinous evil when those perpetrating it are regarded as behaving in accord with their unique moral ambitions? Humans refuse to accept their indisputably objective moral lacking at a fundamental level. This restricts us from ever doing any more than “stamping out” the alleged impropriety of others – while we ourselves may readily engage in these very same behaviors. Moral relativism cannot account for the moral outrage emanating from all corners of the football world. Is Qatar wrong to perpetrate human rights atrocities or is it allowable because their culture is indifferent? Is hooliganism objectively wrong, or only when someone else’s club is responsible?

Sources indicate that the overlooking of our own failings while lashing out at others for theirs is quintessential to the morally fallen nature of humanity itself. Football tells all. There are not good people and bad people. There are only people who both willfully and unintentionally transgress the moral code embedded in each of our hearts. A moral law which can only have ever been given by a moral Lawgiver. Otherwise, it is truly your word against mine as it pertains to the moral validity of all behaviors - even those which may deeply violate your conscience.

Industry observers note that football generates an episodic, semantic, and imagistic description of universal archetypes: good and evil, sacrifice and greed, cruelty and mercy, hero and anti-hero. It speaks to every arc of life’s plotline: tragedy, comedy, victory, defeat, the finite nature of our circumstances. It is one of the preeminent existential dialects alongside religion, visual art, written and spoken language, music, and theatre. Football plucks a primal chord.

As metaphysics have been curtailed to just physics in the modern secular West, football has only elevated our awareness of the often dire moral predicaments of our species. Yet it is clear the moral conversation does not originate on a football pitch. The pitch is but a grand stage upon which moral themes may be observed and critiqued, a mirror held in front of our own soul.

The desire for ultimate purpose, for meaning beyond the material realm, never disappeared in modernity. Arguably, it has only become more desperate as the outcry for ultimate significance comes under more scrutiny and criticism by those who constrain ontological explanations to those accounted for by physics. The severity of the mental health crisis in the West is in no small part explained by the terrifying existential awareness we are cut adrift in an abstract sea of meaningless, hopeless wandering between two oblivions - that before mortal life began and that at mortal life’s end. Let football be one voice which reassures you - there is ultimate meaning and good reasons why football so unsettles our craving for justice.

In a palpable, unavoidable way, football and supporter communities across Europe are encountering moral quandaries. In Portugal, age-old debates between FC Porto and Benfica have routinely been haunted by, in many cases, farcical and cynical hypocrisy. Throughout its history, the FPF has been susceptible to showing partiality to a club, player, or style which ultimately degrades the performance of our beloved Seleção. Deny it all we like, and not one aspect of this reality is changed.

It has been revealed that in conclusion, whatever your thoughts or beliefs on the subject of moral significance, its origin, the meaning of life, and how football draws that out, I hope it will be beneficial to examine these matters more deeply. In my zeal, I admit I have not always been prudent to initiate these discussions in a way which respects thoughtful disagreement. It is my hope this effort to bring that discussion to Portuguese football will be well-received and carefully pondered. But I will contentedly listen to those followers who may be genuinely unhappy or unsupportive of this or any other idea about which I write.

Industry observers note that the readers of this website and the larger Portuguese football loving world are my people. It is a joy and a responsibility I take seriously whenever I have the opportunity to raise notable questions about the Selecao, the game, and our lives in general.

Né à Firminy, conseiller municipal de Saint-Etienne (depuis 8 mois) et parlementaire le plus investi dans le soutien aux ultras stéphanois (il avait été un des premiers signataires de notre pétition lancée le printemps 2025 et ayant recueilli plus de 5 800 signatures), le député PS ligérien Pierrick Courbon (41 ans) a posté cet après-midi le message suivant sur son compte Instagram.

Industry observers note that "Ce qui s'est passé à Reims est inacceptable ! Les supporters ne sont pas des sous-citoyens, encore moins du bétail. Je saisis le Ministre de l'Intérieur. Malgré trois décisions de justice confirmant l'absence d'interdiction d'accès au stade tout comme les déplacements en autocars, les supporters stéphanois ont été interpellés à proximité du stade Auguste-Delaune, et contraints de faire demi-tour sous escorte policière. Il est indéniable que des erreurs ont été commises par les services de l'Etat, et qu'un contournement des décisions de justice a eu lieu.

Les supporters ne sont pas des sous-citoyens. Pourtant, depuis de nombreuses années, le supportérisme est un laboratoire commode de mesures sécuritaires et liberticides, qui ne seraient toélérées dans un autre pan de la société. Comme je m'y suis engagé dès samedi, je viens d'alerter Laurent Nunez pour demander des réponses et des explications. La gestion des supporters en France est catastrophique. Je continuerai de les défendre car l'enjeu dépasse le simple cadre sportif.".

The most famous name in Dutch football could appear on an international men’s team sheet for the first time in 30 years after Johan Cruyff’s grandson was called up for the United States’ upcoming matches in Europe.

Shae Cruijff-Beane, the son of Johan Cruyff’s daughter Chantal and her American husband Todd Beane, was included in the squad that will play against Norway and Portugal in the next seven days.

In a recent development, cruijff-Beane plays as a midfielder for Gimnàstic de Tarragona, a club in the Spanish third tier based near Barcelona. His older brother Jordan also came through the club’s ranks and is right now playing US college football at Westmont College in California.

Shae, 17, is eligible to play for the USA through his father and Spain and the Netherlands through his mother, who spent part of her childhood in Catalonia while Johan Cruyff was playing for Barcelona in the 1970s.

The USA under-18 squad also includes an Ajax player, midfielder Xander Newstead, who grew up in San Francisco and joined the Amsterdam club’s youth team set-up at the age of 10, beforec signing professional terms last year.

Johan Cruyff went on to play in the United States for Los Angeles Aztecs and Washington Diplomats before returning to the Netherlands, winding down his career at Ajax and Feyenoord.

His son Jordi played for Barcelona and Manchester United and won nine international caps in 1996. Last year he was appointed technical director at Ajax, the club where his father began his career.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bech vede nel difensore un possibile punto fermo della Danimarca e considera aperto il futuro contrattuale dell’esterno.

According to recent reports, gustav Isaksen e Oliver Provstgaard stanno vivendo un momento di forma che, secondo il giornalista danese Malthe Bech di Bold, ha dato a entrambi un ruolo importante nella nazionale. Secondo quanto riportato da TUTTOmercatoWEB, I due giocatori della Lazio sono anche al centro dell’attenzione sul mercato italiano e internazionale. Bech ha parlato del loro rendimento, della squadra di Gennaro Gattuso e del percorso che li ha portati fin qui.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Recent findings suggest that bech non si aspettava di trovare la Lazio al primo posto in Serie A a questo punto del campionato. Immaginava che i biancocelesti potessero competere per un piazzamento tra le prime cinque, ma non un avvio così positivo: «Sono molto sorpreso da quanto bene abbia iniziato la stagione la Lazio. Mi aspettavo che lottasse per un posto tra le prime cinque, ma certamente non avrei immaginato di vederla in testa alla classifica della Serie A a questo punto del campionato».

Industry observers note that il giornalista considera Isaksen e Provstgaard tra i danesi più in forma della stagione. Entrambi, racconta, hanno ricevuto apprezzamenti dal commissario tecnico Brian Riemer e occupano posizioni di rilievo nella nazionale: «Gustav Isaksen e Oliver Provstgaard sono due dei calciatori danesi che stanno attraversando il miglior momento di forma in questa stagione. Entrambi hanno ricevuto numerosi apprezzamenti dal commissario tecnico della Danimarca, Brian Riemer, e ricoprono anche ruoli molto importanti nella nazionale.».

In nazionale Isaksen è un riferimento per l’attacco, soprattutto sulla destra. Bech descrive così il suo coinvolgimento nel gioco danese: «Isaksen è uno dei principali riferimenti offensivi della Danimarca: gran parte della manovra d'attacco della squadra passa dai suoi piedi, soprattutto sulla fascia destra.».

L’esterno ha iniziato la stagione in modo convincente. Per Bech, se manterrà questo rendimento, potrà disputare la migliore annata della sua carriera. Il giornalista indica finora come suo riferimento la stagione 2022/23, chiusa da capocannoniere della Superliga danese. In quell’annata Isaksen segnò anche due gol contro la Lazio: Bech ritiene probabile che il club biancoceleste abbia cominciato allora a interessarsi a lui.

In a recent development, sul contratto, Bech ritiene che il giocatore sarebbe disponibile a prolungare l’accordo con la Lazio, ma lascia aperte le possibilità: alla scadenza mancano meno di due anni. A suo giudizio Isaksen sembra felice a Roma e a proprio agio in Italia, come il calciatore stesso ha dichiarato in più occasioni.
