📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A Bundesliga battle between two teams desperate to snap poor runs of form ended in favor of the Bavarian Swabian hosts. Two matchdays into the current Bundesliga campaign, Manuel Baum’s Augsburg were celebrating their status as the top team in the table. Unfortunately, Baum’s Fuggerstädter then proceeded to go seven league fixtures without a win. That streak is now history following a 3-1 home win over Mainz.

Industry observers note that the hosts entered Sunday’s encounter hovering just above the relegation zone, three places below Urs Fischer’s Mainz. Fischer’s team nevertheless only possessed one point more and counted as one of the biggest disappointments of the German top flight. The Rheinhessen traveled to Bavaria on a four-match losing streak, including a loss to 2. Bundesliga outfit Bochum that dumped them out of the Pokal in the second round.

Baum, already dealing with a banged-up defensive corps, had to contend with more bad news this week in the form of injuries to central defenders Chrislain Matsima and Jeffrey Gouweleeuw. Matsima’s absence forced the FCA trainer to hand 18-year-old prospect Tim Schnitzer his Bundesliga starting XI debut. Captain Gouweleeuw, meanwhile, could luckily enough be replaced by Manchester City loanee Juma Bah, who had returned from suspension. Schnitzer and Bah were among five changes to the starting XI Baum employed in the recent 5-2 away defeat to RB Leipzig. Marius Wolf, Michael Gregoritsch, and Alexis Claude-Maurice started over Han-Noah Massengo, Arijon Ibrahimovic, and Rodrigo Ribeiro.

Sources indicate that fischer too needed to pull the trigger on several changes. Though the Mainz trainer declared himself largely satisfied with the performance of his team in a narrow loss against Bayern Munich just prior to the international break, four latest outfielders took to the pitch for the Rheinhessen. Fischer, having several of his preferred starters back, sent Phillip Tietz, Phillipp Mwene, Paul Nebel, and Stefan Posch onto the field in place of Ransford Königsdörffer, Silvan Widmer, Jae-Sung Lee, and Fabio Gruber. Posch returned from suspension after getting sent off in a disastrous encounter against Elversberg that saw Fischer’s charges dispatched 4-1.

Recent findings suggest that baum’s changes certainly produced attractive football in the opening stages. Wolf’s placement as the right wingback enabled the reliably versatile Robin Fellhauer to slide inside and work in the packed midfield alongside Fabian Rieder, Claude-Maurice, and Anton Kade. This particular FCA foursome strode forward with reckless abandon, mostly keeping Mainz pinned back in their own half throughout the entire first quarter-of-an-hour. Sharp combos involving the midfield and the wingbacks produced plenty of incursions into the FSV penalty area. Kade unfortunately couldn’t find the right angle on the best of the opportunities to score, shooting well wide from only six meters out in the 12th minute.

Industry observers note that the opener finally came on Augsburg’s second corner of the afternoon. A quality free-kick from Claude-Maurice was actually shepherded out into touch deftly by former FCA striker Phillip Tietz in the 19th minute. Newly minted FCA record holder Gregoritsch was able to convert the subsequent set-piece for the 1-0. Makeshift Augsburg defender Yannik Keitel did an excellent job beating Mainz’s Kaishu Sano in an aerial duel after Rieder swung in the corner from the right. Keitel’s header was initially saved by Robin Zentner, who parried the ball toward the far post. The rebound fell perfectly for the onrushing Gregoritsch, who easily slid in his sixth Bundesliga goal of the campaign. As Baum and his crew knew full well, however, an early lead meant little.

It has been revealed that in their ongoing seven-game winless run, Augsburg had actually squandered the lead in six of them. On five occasions, Baum’s team scored the opening goal of the match. Some five minutes after Gregoritsch opened the scoring, it appeared as if another lead was almost certain to evaporate. Somehow, one of Mainz’s most dependable scorers spurned a chance to equalize. Tietz found himself free in front of goal in the 24th off a blitz counter, but blasted the ball well over the bar in front of his former FanKurve. Apart from that chance, the Bavarian Swabian hosts did still remain the more active side.

According to recent reports, the 2-0 finally came off yet another corner from the right in the 36th minute. This time, fellow fresh starter Bah would bundle home another Rieder corner when Mainz couldn’t get the service from the right clear. Amid all the jostling prior to Bah bundling the ball home, the second goal withstood VAR scrutiny. Regrettably, the rest of the half would fall prey to officiating controversies. A sequence of events shortly after the second goal rapidly led to match official Martin Petersen losing control of the match.

Recent findings suggest that augsburg thought they had scored the 3-0 in the 41st minute when Keitel slotted home off a quick throw-in. Petersen nevertheless ruled that FCA defender Bah had fouled Mainz counterpart Kacper Potulski in the lead-up. Petersen showed restraint by not booking the crowd of Augsburg players who stood before him to protest his decision, but offered head coach Baum no such quarter when he kept Nadiem Amiri from executing a throw-in in the 43rd. Baum kept the ball himself whilst protesting to Petersen. The FCA trainer was promptly ejected from proceedings on a straight red.

Recent findings suggest that petersen found himself at the center of more protests from players before it was time to head into the tunnel. The hosts were not pleased when the referee declined to whistle for a shove by Posch on Claude-Maurice just outside the box during first-half injury time. Prior to that, Petersen was compelled by VAR to take another look at a Fellhauer foul on Sano in the 44th. Petersen initially only awarded a yellow card despite the fact that Fellhauer caught Sano on the knee with his swinging boot. Petersen stood by his decision and was surely pleased to retreat to the tunnel after a heated, scrappy, and contentious end to the half.

To the relief of most observers, the focus returned to football after the change of ends. There would be no controversy attached to either of the goals scored in the opening five minutes of the second half. The hosts added their third goal shortly after play resumed. A free-kick delivery from the right was initially cleared before Behrens headed the ball back into the penalty area. Wolf helped it onward, and Posch inadvertently glanced the ball into Gregoritsch’s path in the 48th minute. The Austrian striker stroked home the 3-0. Fischer’s team responded by pulling a goal back promptly, with halftime sub Königsdörffer polishing off a nice distance effort on a quick counter three minutes later.

In a recent development, königsdörffer’s 3-1 worked wonders for the carnival club’s confidence, and Fischer’s men undeniably looked more assured heading forward for the duration of proceedings. Mainz tightened up the possession statistics and looked more inspired when forging ahead. The more optically pleasing football from Mainz nevertheless didn’t end up producing another goal or even another memorable attempt on target. Instead, it was Augsburg who looked more dangerous on the counter. FCA sub Uchenna Ogundu unluckily missed out on the 4-1 with a strike off the inside of the far post in the 81st.

Finn Dahmen (5) – Juma Bah (6), Yannik Keitel (6), Tim Schnitzer (6) – Marius Wolf (6), Robin Fellhauer (6), Fabian Rieder (6), Hennes Behrens (5) – Anton Kade (6), Alexis Claude-Maurice (5) – Michael Gregoritsch (7).

Substitutes: Arijon Ibrahimovic (6), Uchenna Ogundu (6), Young-Woo Seol (-), Mert Kömür (-).

Robin Zentner (4) – Danny da Costa (5), Stefan Posch (1), Kacper Potulski (6), Anthony Caci (5) – Kaishu Sano (5), Phillipp Mwene (6) – Paul Nebel (4), Nadiem Amiri (3), Sheraldo Becker (4) – Phillip Tietz (4).

Substitutes: Ransford Königsdörffer (7), Benedict Hollerbach (6), Silvan Widmer (6), Eric Martel (-), Rael Nakuzola (-).

According to recent reports, the Austrian international proved the difference-maker with an exceptionally efficient performance in front of goal. Gregoritsch scored twice from just three shots, putting both of his efforts on target past Robin Zentner and outperforming his 1.36 xG. The 31-year-old wasn’t particularly involved in Augsburg’s build-up play, registering just 26 touches and completing 56 percent of his passes during his 72 minutes on the pitch. Gregoritsch nevertheless demonstrated precisely why Baum continues to place his faith in him. The veteran striker’s opportunistic finishing on both goals helped Augsburg snap their seven-match winless streak and lifted his Bundesliga tally to six goals for the season.

GGFN | Peter Weis – reporting from the WWK Arena.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that eighteen-year-old FC Augsburg academy prospect Tim Schnitzer enjoyed an unforgettable afternoon on Sunday, making his first Bundesliga start in his hometown club’s 3-1 victory over Mainz 05. A defensive injury crisis forced head coach Manuel Baum to deploy the youngster in an unfamiliar role, but Schnitzer delivered an impressively composed performance that earned special praise from his trainer.

According to recent reports, speaking to Get German Football News and other journalists in the mixed zone after the match, Schnitzer called it a “dream come true to start where I used to be a ball boy”. The Augsburg native admitted to some nervousness ahead of his starting XI debut. Schnitzer revealed that he had slept less than usual the night before and even awoken before his alarm clock.

“I was definitely a little nervous,” Schnitzer conceded.

The Germany youth international nevertheless settled into his role on the left side of Augsburg’s back-three relatively promptly, displaying maturity and confidence in possession. Schnitzer won 70 percent of his ground challenges and connected with 89 percent of his passes, according to Opta data.

GGFN considered Schnitzer and the rest of the makeshift back-three (consisting of Schnitzer’s fellow out-of-position player Yannik Keitel and young Man City loanee Juma Bah) worthy of above average marks in our player ratings piece.

“When you seize your chance, you become more and more integrated into the team,” Schnitzer remarked in the mixed zone.

In a recent development, augsburg’s defensive personnel shortage left Baum with little choice but to turn to the 18-year-old, who ordinarily operates as a defensive midfielder. Chrislain Matsima, Jeffrey Gouweleeuw, Noahkai Banks, and Calvin Brackelmann were all unavailable, leaving the returning Juma Bah as the only other natural central defender available to the FCA trainer.

“We were missing four central defenders and were still able to field a back-three,” Baum remarked at the post-match press conference. “And I believe we were able to implement something that we always aim for as a club. Namely, to integrate young players in at the right moment. And we witnessed that with Tim Schnitzer, who delivered a fabulous performance in his first game and the team really helped him out with that.”.

“A huge compliment to the whole team,” Baum continued near the end of his opening press conference statement. “And let’s single out Tim again. He’s from our own academy and has been with us since the U9s. I think he grew up just a couple of blocks away from the academy. I think we can be very happy about the result, the team, and the next homegrown talent who was able to start today.”.

Recent findings suggest that schnitzer’s first Bundesliga start represents another significant milestone in a development pathway that Get German Football News has followed closely since the summer. The Augsburg-born midfielder made his senior debut against RB Leipzig last March before spending the summer attempting to establish himself as a genuine first-team option. Schnitzer’s versatility emerged as one of his most promising qualities, with the youngster capable of operating as a defensive midfielder, central defender, or No. 8.

Baum had already identified Schnitzer as one of Augsburg’s most promising academy graduates in August, even mentioning the teenager among several FCA players he hoped might eventually attract Germany senior national-team consideration. Our 2026/27 Augsburg tactical preview also highlighted Schnitzer’s encouraging preseason performances, including his goal against Bournemouth, and suggested that the youngster should have opportunities to collect meaningful Bundesliga minutes.

In a recent development, sunday’s injury-enforced selection certainly provided one such opportunity. Schnitzer responded by completing the entire 90 minutes and helping Augsburg end their seven-match winless streak. Whether the teenager retains his place once Augsburg’s established defenders return remains to be seen. Baum nevertheless has another option at his disposal, and the youngster who once served as a ball boy at the WWK Arena has taken another crucial step toward becoming a Bundesliga regular.

GGFN | Peter Weis – reporting from the WWK Arena.

Florian Wirtz scores twice (including a stunner) as Germany thump Netherlands 5-0 in UEFA Nations League... as Liverpool misfit receives a hug from Jurgen Klopp after impressing

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 17:56 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 19:19 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz scored a stunning brace for Germany as Jurgen Klopp's side thumped the Netherlands in the Nations League.
  • The 23-year-old has had a tough time of it at Anfield since his £116million move to the club last summer, but has never really struggled on the international stage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 17:56 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 19:19 EST, 16 November 2026.

Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz scored a stunning brace for Germany as Jurgen Klopp's side thumped the Netherlands in the Nations League.

The 23-year-old has had a tough time of it at Anfield since his £116million move to the club last summer, but has never really struggled on the international stage.

And he continued that trend on Monday evening with two goals for his side to help them top their Nations League group.

It has been revealed that his first was the pick of the bunch. Wirtz moved along the forward line as a Dutch side without Virgil van Dijk struggled to contain him. He picked up the ball around 25 yards out, cut inside onto his weaker left foot, and curled a pearling effort into the far corner off the post.

That goal, which came on the hour mark, put his side 2-0 up after Freiburg's Derry Scherhant had scored the opener, and Wirtz wasn't done there.

Centre back Nico Schlotterbeck made it 3-0 before the Liverpool man picked up his second of the night after drifting into the penalty box unmarked and finishing high after good work from Brajan Gruda.

Sources indicate that cette version de Wirtz avec le maillot de la Mannschaft c’est celle qu’on aimerait voir chaque semaine en PL. Quel missile pour faire le break ! Meilleur buteur allemand sur cette édition de l’UNL. 🇩🇪🔥 pic.twitter.com/m0DqaOungS.

Florian Wirtz scored a brace for Germany as they thumped the Netherlands 5-0 in Nations League action.

Liverpool midfielder Wirtz received a big hug from a smiling Jurgen Klopp at full time.

Gruda himself, who is on loan at RB Leipzig from Brighton, wrapped up the five-star win on a night that arguably saw Klopp announce himself as Germany boss.

After full-time, the ex-Liverpool manager gave Wirtz a huge hug as the duo beamed with substantial smiles on their faces.

While it was a night to remember for Germany, a Netherlands team that included the likes of Micky van de Ven, Jurrien Timber and Wirtz's Liverpool team-mate Cody Gakpo were left exasperated.

Van Dijk had pulled out of the squad with a knock after playing with a knock in recent weeks.

His side will still, though, compete in the Nations League quarter-finals after finishing second in the group, finishing ahead of Greece on goal difference.

As for Wirtz, he will hope his performance will help continue what has been an uphill climb so far this season.

He also found the net for Germany in their first match of the international break – a 3-1 win over Serbia – and picked up a goal and assist in Liverpool's 3-1 win over Crystal Palace before the international break.

In total, he has two goals and five assists in 15 games for Liverpool this season – though the Reds will hope those numbers increase as the season goes on.

His second goal came as he drifted into the penalty area and finished high into the net.

Last month, meanwhile, Reds manager Andoni Iraola insisted he has full faith in his midfielder.

Sources indicate that 'I think he has had a little bit of everything this season,' he remarked. 'He has had good games, probably the other day was not his best game, especially offensively. We trust Florian.

Sources indicate that 'Florian is a very good player. He was coming from good performances in the international break, I think. I think it is a matter of everyone to find his moment.'.

Klopp hailed him 'exceptional', meanwhile, during the last international break.

Augsburg’s Manuel Baum questions rulebook’s double standard after seeing red in Bundesliga win

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (394 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • FC Augsburg head coach Manuel Baum has questioned the severity of the straight red card he received during Sunday’s 3-1 Bundesliga victory over Mainz 05, while acknowledging that referee Martin Petersen acted in accordance with the rules.
  • Augsburg, already leading 2-0, thought they had added a third goal when Yannik Keitel finished from close range following a throw-in.
  • “The 3-0 should have been legitimate and in accordance with the rules,” Baum remarked at the post-match press conference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

FC Augsburg head coach Manuel Baum has questioned the severity of the straight red card he received during Sunday’s 3-1 Bundesliga victory over Mainz 05, while acknowledging that referee Martin Petersen acted in accordance with the rules. The FCA trainer was dismissed in the 43rd minute following a heated sequence of events toward the end of the first half.

Augsburg, already leading 2-0, thought they had added a third goal when Yannik Keitel finished from close range following a throw-in. Petersen nevertheless disallowed the goal for a foul on Mainz defender Kacper Potulski in the build-up. Baum’s frustration with the decision ultimately led to his dismissal. The 47-year-old held onto the ball as Mainz midfielder Nadiem Amiri attempted to execute a quick throw-in.

“The 3-0 should have been legitimate and in accordance with the rules,” Baum remarked at the post-match press conference. “We’ve been informed afterwards that it should have counted. The ball came to me and I held onto it because I wanted to have a word with the ref and, I only noticed on the replay that I moved it from my left to right hand [while Nadiem Amiri was trying to execute a quick throw in].”.

Under IFAB Law 12, a team official who delays the opposition’s restart by holding onto the ball commits a sending-off offence. Players, by contrast, are generally cautioned for delaying a restart. Baum acknowledged that Petersen’s decision was technically correct but suggested that the rules impose an unnecessarily harsh punishment on coaches.

Recent findings suggest that “According to the rules, the coach must be punished draconically in such a case,” Baum continued. “A player would be given a yellow. A coach must automatically be given a red for such a thing. What? I find that a little strange. I think a yellow card would have been sufficient. But, okay. That’s the letter of the law. The team, I think did a great job of disengaging themselves from the emotions in the game and seeing it through.”.

Sources indicate that despite losing their head coach before halftime, Augsburg successfully protected their advantage and ultimately ended a seven-match winless Bundesliga streak. Michael Gregoritsch completed his brace shortly after the restart, and the hosts held firm after Mainz substitute Ransford Königsdörffer pulled a goal back.

GGFN | Peter Weis – reporting from the WWK Arena.
